Package com.egradx.auth

Class EgradxAuthService

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.auth.EgradxAuthService
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.beans.factory.Aware, org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisherAware
public class EgradxAuthService extends Object implements org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisherAware
The single entry point apps built on egradx-sdk call to register, log in, refresh, log out, and validate users — in-process, no separate auth microservice to run or call. See docs/sdk/feature-roadmap.md in egradx-v1-workspace for the ikon-v9/OIMP sources this was distilled from, and EgradxRoleService for how role-based access control works here.

    • register

      @Transactional public EgradxUserDto register(EgradxSignupRequest request)
      Registers a new user with no organization membership and no platform-owner status — both are granted afterwards by whoever's responsible for that (an org admin via EgradxRoleService, or platform-owner bootstrap code), not by this call. There is no self-registration-into-an-organization flow here, matching how OIMP's own equivalent always has *someone else* create a user into a specific organization rather than a user signing themselves into one.
      Throws:
      DuplicateResourceException - if the username or email is already taken

    • login

      public EgradxAuthResult login(EgradxLoginRequest request)
      Verifies credentials, resolves which organization the resulting session is scoped to, and issues an access + refresh token pair.

      Organization resolution: a platform-owner user is never scoped to an organization (request.organizationId() is ignored for them). Otherwise: if request.organizationId() is given, the user must actually have a membership there. If it's omitted, and the user has exactly one membership, that one is used automatically; zero memberships logs them in with no organization/authorities at all (not an error — they just haven't been added to one yet); more than one requires the caller to specify which, via ValidationException.

      Throws:
      AuthenticationException - if the username doesn't exist, is deactivated, or the password doesn't match (the same message in every case, so a caller can't use this to enumerate valid usernames), or if the resolved organization is suspended
      ValidationException - if the user belongs to more than one organization and request.organizationId() wasn't given
      AuthorizationException - if request.organizationId() was given but the user isn't a member of it

      AuthorizationException - if they are not a member of organizationId, or it is suspended

    • logout

      @Transactional public void logout(EgradxRefreshTokenRequest request)
      Soft-revokes a refresh token (logout) — a no-op, not an error, if it doesn't exist or was already revoked, so this never leaks whether a given token value was ever valid.

    • validateToken

      public EgradxUserTokenContext validateToken(String accessToken)
      Verifies an access token issued by login(com.egradx.auth.dto.EgradxLoginRequest)/refreshAccessToken(com.egradx.auth.dto.EgradxRefreshTokenRequest) and returns its decoded claims. Its organizationId is non-authoritative (see that field's javadoc) — for an actual authorization decision use EgradxPermissionResolver/ EgradxTenantContext, which re-derive everything fresh from the database rather than trusting the token.
      Throws:
      AuthenticationException - if the token is missing, malformed, expired, or fails signature/issuer verification.
